claims.claimText: Waterloo AVPA guidance on Applying UW Principles of AI Enablement to Teaching and Learning states that GenAI use must consider data security, prohibiting uploading student work or course materials to insecure AI tools, and specifying that student information such as identification or grades is subject to Policy 46 (Information Management) and must not be uploaded to AI tools that do not meet institutional security requirements.
claims.claimValue: Student work, course materials, and student information (Policy 46) must not be uploaded to insecure AI tools.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: GenAI use in teaching and learning must consider the security of student data, course materials, and other intellectual property. Instructors and students must select AI tools that provide an appropriate level of data protection, following university guidance. Neither course materials nor student work should be uploaded to insecure AI tools that might share them without permission. Student information such as identification or grades is subject to Policy 46 – Information Management and must not be uploaded to AI tools that do not meet institutional security requirements.

AVPA teaching guidance prohibits uploading student work or course materials to insecure AI tools.
IST matrix establishes tools may be approved only for specific uses, configurations, or user groups.
Academic integrity guidelines instruct educators to be explicit regarding whether GenAI is allowed.
IST review processes assess security, privacy, and contractual risks for tools using University data.
Graduate students must obtain permission from supervisor or advisory committee for GenAI use.
Deploying AI systems processing University data requires Information Risk Assessment and Steward approval.
Graduate guidance directs students to consult supervisors regarding limits and scope of GenAI.
AVPA course-outline sample language allows GenAI when documentation, citation, and acknowledgement are provided.

gaps: AVPA course outline language represents optional instructor syllabus templates, not blanket campus-wide student AI clearance.
Copilot Basic is available under Waterloo accounts, but student pricing and eligibility for Copilot Premium or specialized licenses remain an unverified gap.
Deploying AI-enabled systems processing University data requires Information Risk Assessment and Information Steward approval; general student procurement tariffs remain unverified.
Formal investigation workflows, sanction outcome schedules, and appeal procedures under Waterloo Policy 71 are not fully evidenced by the instructor expectation guidance excerpt.

cl-university-of-waterloo-microsoft-copi.text: Microsoft Copilot is listed for University of Waterloo in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: not specified.

evidence.quote: Waterloo IST says Microsoft Copilot is currently available through a UWaterloo account; access automatically provides personal and company data protection.

cl-waterloo-avpa-student-data-protection.text: Waterloo AVPA guidance on Applying UW Principles of AI Enablement to Teaching and Learning states that GenAI use must consider data security, prohibiting uploading student work or course materials to insecure AI tools, and specifying that student information such as identification or grades is subject to Policy 46 (Information Management) and must not be uploaded to AI tools that do not meet institutional security requirements.

evidence.quote: GenAI use in teaching and learning must consider the security of student data, course materials, and other intellectual property. Instructors and students must select AI tools that provide an appropriate level of data protection, following university guidance. Neither course materials nor student work should be uploaded to insecure AI tools that might share them without permission. Student information such as identification or grades is subject to Policy 46 – Information Management and must not be uploaded to AI tools that do not meet institutional security requirements.
evidence.location: Safe & fair use: Responsible, ethical, inclusive AI

claim-waterloo-ist-ai-tool-data-approval.text: Waterloo IST tells users to confirm whether an AI tool is listed and approved for the intended type of University data before using it with University data.

evidence.quote: first confirm whether the tool is listed and approved below for the type of University data you intend to use.
evidence.location: Approved AI tools

claim-waterloo-ai-instructor-rules.text: Waterloo's Academic Integrity page says instructors should state whether AI tools such as ChatGPT are allowed for assignments, tests, or exams, and that students who do not follow those instructor rules are subject to Policy 71 academic-misconduct processes.

evidence.quote: At present, it's important for instructors to be explicit about whether artificial intelligence or tools like ChatGPT are allowed to be used to complete assignments, tests or exams, and if so, the extent to which it is allowed, and if it should be cited and how to cite it. A student who does not comply with the instructor's rules about the use of such tools will be subject to Policy 71 and an investigation into academic misconduct.
evidence.location: Instructor resources for Artificial Intelligence ChatGPT tools

claim-waterloo-ist-review-risks.text: Waterloo IST says review processes assess AI tools used with University data for security, privacy, and contractual risks.

evidence.quote: These review processes ensure that any AI tool used with University data is assessed for security, privacy, and contractual risks, whether the tool is standalone, embedded, or part of an AI-enabled system.
evidence.location: Approval & Support

claim-waterloo-grad-genai-permission.text: Waterloo's graduate-student GenAI guidance says graduate students should not submit GenAI-produced work for course assignments without explicit course-instructor permission or instruction.

evidence.quote: Without explicit permission or instruction from the course instructor, students should never submit work produced by any of the GenAI tools.
evidence.location: Academic and professional integrity

claim-waterloo-ist-ai-system-deployment.text: For units or individuals deploying AI-enabled systems that process University data, Waterloo IST says projects must undergo an Information Risk Assessment and receive Information Steward approval before using University data.

evidence.quote: All AI-enabled system projects must undergo an Information Risk Assessment (IRA). A Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) may also be required, depending on the nature of the data being collected or processed. Approval from the appropriate Information Steward is required before using any University data, even if that data is publicly available.
evidence.location: Key Requirements

claim-waterloo-grad-research-consultatio.text: For graduate research contexts, Waterloo's GenAI guidance directs graduate students to consult supervisors and, when applicable, advisory committees about the limits and scope of GenAI-tool use.

evidence.quote: For research, graduate students should consult with their supervisor(s) and advisory committee (if one exists) about the limit and scope of the use of GenAI tools, which is often discipline-dependent. Permitted uses and expectations for using GenAI tools should be communicated between the students and their supervisor(s).
evidence.location: Academic and professional integrity

claim-waterloo-course-outline-permitted-.text: Waterloo's AVPA course-outline suggestions include sample language for instructors who permit GenAI use, specifying that such use may be allowed for assignments with proper documentation, citation, and acknowledgement.

evidence.quote: For instructors who permit generative AI use: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) trained using large language models (LLM) or other methods to produce text, images, music, or code, like Chat GPT, DALL-E, or GitHub CoPilot, may be used for assignments in this class with proper documentation, citation, and acknowledgement.
evidence.location: For instructors who permit generative AI use
